details.description: Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings, launched October 28, 2025 as part of the Nova 2 family, is Amazon's embedding model for agentic retrieval-augmented generation and semantic search. It maps images and audio into a single unified vector space so applications can run cross-modal vector search, and it offers four selectable output dimension sizes and asynchronous batch inference for large-scale jobs.
advantages: Unifies image and audio into one semantic space, enabling cross-modal vector search from a single model (AWS Amazon Nova 2 user guide).
Offers four output dimension sizes -- 3072, 1024, 384 or 256 -- to trade off embedding accuracy against vector storage cost (AWS Amazon Nova 2 user guide).
Supports asynchronous batch inference with built-in segmentation for long audio inputs (AWS Amazon Nova 2 user guide).
disadvantages: Maximum context length is 8K tokens per input, or 30 seconds per audio segment (AWS Amazon Nova 2 user guide).
Does not support the Converse, Chat Completions or InvokeModel APIs; access on the bedrock-runtime endpoint is limited to the asynchronous StartAsyncInvoke API (AWS Bedrock model card).
use_cases: Large-scale batch embedding of audio via the asynchronous API

notes: Catalog facts list modality as audio_input, image_input only; the maker's own embeddings page additionally documents text, document and video input support. That gap is real, but the researched file had actually written text/documents/video into the description, two advantages and two use cases despite saying in this field that none of it was added -- those mentions were removed so the file matches its own stated approach; the gap is only flagged here now. Separately, the Bedrock model card's APIs-supported table marks InvokeModel as unsupported (only StartAsyncInvoke is checked) for this model, contradicting the file's disadvantage claim that InvokeModel is available and contradicting the synchronous invoke_model() code sample on the Nova 2 user guide's embeddings page; the model card was treated as authoritative for API support and the description's 'synchronous ... batch inference' claim was corrected to asynchronous-only accordingly. No MTEB or other accuracy-style benchmark scores were found on any page opened, so evaluations is empty.
